raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`DotsToolDetector.detect_and_parse` finds tool-call blocks with

```python
r"<dots_function_call>\s*(.*?)\s*</dots_function_call>"
```

When the model emits the opening marker but never the closing one, `\s*`, the lazy `(.*?)` and the second `\s*` backtrack over every split of a whitespace run, so the match is **cubic** in the run length:

| Input | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `<dots_function_call>` + 2,000 newlines (~2 KB) | 12.8 s | 0.4 ms |
| `<dots_function_call>` + 200,000 newlines | hours (extrapolated) | 0.1 ms |
| 14 KB fuzzer-found input | 54.3 s | 0.1 ms |

Tool-call parsing runs synchronously on the tokenizer manager's event loop, so a single such response, which a user can elicit through the prompt, stalls every in-flight request on the server.

Found with an Atheris coverage-guided fuzzing harness over all tool-call detectors, which records per-input parse time.

## Modifications

- Replace the regex with a linear `str.find` scan over complete `bot ... eot` blocks, the same approach `parse_streaming_increment` in this detector already uses. `_parse_block` already `.strip()`s each body, so the `\s*` around the group never affected results.
- Add a bug-regression test: a complete call followed by an unclosed marker and 20k newlines must parse in < 1 s and still return the complete call. It takes > 90 s on `main` and ~1 ms with this change.

## Accuracy Tests

No model-output change. `test_dots_detector.py`: 11/11 pass (10 existing + 1 new).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

See the table above. Re-fuzzing the fixed detector (365k executions) found no slow inputs.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (N/A)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

files.patch:
@@ -44,10 +44,6 @@ def __init__(self):
         super().__init__()
         self.bot_token = "<dots_function_call>"
         self.eot_token = "</dots_function_call>"
-        self.func_call_regex = re.compile(
-            rf"{re.escape(self.bot_token)}\s*(.*?)\s*{re.escape(self.eot_token)}",
-            re.DOTALL,
-        )
         self.invoke_regex = re.compile(
             r"<invoke\s+name\s*=\s*(?P<name>[^>]+)>(?P<body>.*?)</invoke>",
             re.DOTALL,
@@ -177,6 +173,18 @@ def _parse_block(self, content: str, tools: list[Tool]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
             raise TypeError("dots JSON tool call must be an object")
         return [parsed]
 
+    def _iter_blocks(self, text: str):
+        # Linear scan on purpose: a `bot\s*(.*?)\s*eot` regex backtracks
+        # cubically over whitespace when the end marker never arrives.
+        start = text.find(self.bot_token)
+        while start != -1:
+            content_start = start + len(self.bot_token)
+            end = text.find(self.eot_token, content_start)
+            if end == -1:
+                return
+            yield text[content_start:end]
+            start = text.find(self.bot_token, end + len(self.eot_token))
+
     def has_tool_call(self, text: str) -> bool:
         return self.bot_token in text
 
@@ -186,9 +194,9 @@ def detect_and_parse(self, text: str, tools: list[Tool]) -> StreamingParseResult
             return StreamingParseResult(normal_text=text)
 
         calls: list[ToolCallItem] = []
-        for block in self.func_call_regex.finditer(text):
+        for block in self._iter_blocks(text):
             try:
-                for parsed in self._parse_block(block.group(1), tools):
+                for parsed in self._parse_block(block, tools):
                     calls.extend(self.parse_base_json(parsed, tools))
             except (json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError, TypeError) as exc:
                 logger.warning("Failed to parse dots tool call: %s", exc)

@@ -1,4 +1,5 @@
 import json
+import time
 import unittest
 
 from sglang.srt.entrypoints.openai.protocol import Function, Tool
@@ -108,6 +109,24 @@ def test_non_stream_supports_multiple_invokes_and_json_fallback(self):
             ],
         )
 
+    def test_non_stream_unclosed_block_with_whitespace_parses_in_linear_time(self):
+        """An unclosed marker followed by a whitespace run must not stall the
+        parser (it runs on the event loop), and earlier complete calls survive."""
+        tools = [_tool("search", {"query": {"type": "string"}})]
+        parser = FunctionCallParser(tools, "dots")
+        text = (
+            '<dots_function_call>\n{"name":"search","arguments":{"query":"a"}}\n'
+            "</dots_function_call><dots_function_call>" + "\n" * 20000
+        )
+
+        start = time.perf_counter()
+        _, calls = parser.parse_non_stream(text)
+        elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start
+
+        self.assertLess(elapsed, 1.0)
+        self.assertEqual([call.name for call in calls], ["search"])
+        self.assertEqual(json.loads(calls[0].parameters), {"query": "a"})
+
     def test_streaming_buffers_partial_marker_and_emits_all_complete_calls(self):
         tools = [_tool("search", {"query": {"type": "string"}})]
